messages:
lena (devex): throwing this here since the Go sample app used in onboarding hangs on cancel when our dev auth hook rotates tokens mid-stream. small repro but pretty blocking for new users.

lena (devex): steps: start generator stream, wait for auth refresh (simulated TTL), then cancel parent ctx. Recv goroutine keeps running.

lena (devex): minimal snippet:
```go
ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 10*time.Second)
stream, err := client.GeneratorStream(ctx, req)
if err != nil { return err }
go func() {
  for {
    tok, err := stream.Recv()
    if err != nil { log.Printf("recv done: %v", err); return }
    // handle tok
  }
}()
// simulate auth refresh then cancel()
cancel() // returns, but goroutine often stays alive when token rotated
```

rafael (go-sdk): thanks lena. this rings a bell  we recently added an auth refresh flow that swaps the HTTP transport. If Recv() is blocked on an internal channel and the transport swap doesn't close that channel, goroutine can be orphaned.

rafael (go-sdk): quick design thoughts: we should expose both a per-call ctx (Recv(ctx)) and a Close() on stream. Recv() can remain but should delegate to Recv(context.Background()) so we don't break callers. Also ensure internal recv loops select on ctx.Done().

ethan (runtime): on runtime side, when we hot-swap transport we currently attempt a graceful drain but only wait on a global waitGroup. That doesn't tie to the stream's context. I'll change swap to: create per-stream cancelable child context, cancel it before replacing transport, and close the recv channels.

lena (devex): can we also surface a small note in the onboarding sample app README? new users easily copy that pattern and miss per-Recv cancellation. a 2-line recommended snippet would save a lot of confusion.

zoe (onboarding): agreed. I'll add a "Cancellation best practice" section with a small example showing context.WithTimeout + defer stream.Close() and a note about token rotation causing short-lived retries.

rafael (go-sdk): for backward compatibility I'll add RecvWithContext(ctx) and implement Recv() as RecvWithContext(context.Background()). Also add stream.Close() to signal EOF to recv loop. Planning to open a PR after lunch.

ethan (runtime): I'll add a flaky-transport unit that forces token TTL=1s and simulates transport swap while Cancel happens; CI will fail until we fix. Sam (SRE) saw increased goroutine counts on similar.

ci-bot: ci: go-sdk/generator:pr-3301 queued  flaky-transport-cancel test scheduled.

lena (devex): perfect. one more UX ask: could the sample app include a small test harness that intentionally rotates tokens so onboarding users can run it locally and see correct cancellation behavior? would be a great learning tool.

zoe (onboarding): yep i'll add that to the quickstart. thanks all :thumbsup:

rafael (go-sdk): assigning PR to @ethan for runtime changes and @zoe for sample update.
